note: The outside modules bin/vh uses: programs, packages, models, services and agents that others maintain, each behind a thin adapter here. bin/vh doctor reads this table and says which of them this machine can use (tools/doctor.py; --json, --probe). The fields are in bin/vh doctor -h; a new module gets its entry here in the PR that first calls it (CONTRIBUTING.md, 外接模块). The first_run sizes are those of the wiki's "What gets downloaded" table (Getting Started; measured on macOS arm64, 2026-10-01): keep the two in step when either changes.

modules.name: node
modules.purpose: Runs the page tools (frames, render, patch, textcheck, fonts check, cues, determinism), HyperFrames and the hand-drawn engine.

install.macos: brew install node (or nvm install 22)

modules.name: ffmpeg
modules.purpose: Decodes, encodes, probes and mixes every picture and sound: render and patch encode with libx264, check and mux probe with ffprobe.
modules.license: LGPL-2.1-or-later, GPL when built with libx264 (Homebrew's: GPL-3.0-or-later)

features.missing: no libx264 encoder: render, patch, deliver and proxy encode with it (a GPL build has it: Homebrew's, the distribution's)

install.macos: brew install ffmpeg
install.linux: sudo apt install ffmpeg, or your package manager

modules.name: python3
modules.purpose: Runs most of bin/vh's tools, this doctor among them; the ones with packages run through uv.

install.macos: brew install python (or the Xcode command line tools)

modules.name: uv
modules.purpose: Runs the Python tools with their packages without installing them system-wide (numpy, librosa, pillow, jieba, mlx-audio …), and Manim's per-project environments.

install.macos: brew install uv

modules.name: git
modules.purpose: Fetches the reference repos (references/fetch.sh) and the harness itself (install.sh).

install.macos: xcode-select --install, or brew install git

modules.name: chrome
modules.purpose: The browser the page tools draw with when CHROME_PATH names none and there is no chrome-headless-shell: Google Chrome, Chromium or Playwright's Chromium.
modules.license: Google Chrome: Google's terms; Chromium: BSD-3-Clause

install.macos: install Google Chrome, or set CHROME_PATH
install.linux: sudo apt install chromium, or npx playwright install chromium, or set CHROME_PATH

modules.name: chrome-headless-shell
modules.purpose: The browser hyperframes render uses, at the version HyperFrames pins; the page tools take it first too, so text lays out as in the film.

install.macos: the first HyperFrames render downloads it (about 200 MB), or now: cd styles/_swatch && npx hyperframes browser ensure
install.linux: the first HyperFrames render downloads it (about 200 MB), or now: cd styles/_swatch && npx hyperframes browser ensure

modules.name: hyperframes
modules.purpose: The HTML composition engine of short, promo, data and meme films, and of the style swatches.
adapter: tools/hf.py (its registry at the pin's tag, and its add)

install.macos: cd styles/_swatch && npm ci (each project gets its own through bin/vh new or hf-init)
install.linux: cd styles/_swatch && npm ci (each project gets its own through bin/vh new or hf-init)

modules.name: hyperframes-registry
modules.purpose: HyperFrames' registry of blocks and components at the pinned tag: bin/vh hf catalog reads its registry.json and each item's manifest, hf add the item's files.
modules.license: Apache-2.0, the HyperFrames repository's; an item that names no licence of its own is recorded as the repository's, presumed

needs.account: none: raw.githubusercontent.com needs no key (it answers a burst with 429, so hf reads six items at a time)

modules.name: gsap
modules.purpose: The animation library of HyperFrames compositions; bin/vh hf-init installs the scaffold's version into each project so no render loads it from a CDN.
modules.license: GSAP Standard 'no charge' license (https://gsap.com/standard-license), not an open-source licence

check.per_project: bin/vh hf-init installs 3.14.2 into each HyperFrames project

modules.name: puppeteer-core
modules.purpose: Drives Chrome for the hand-drawn engine's renders and for doctor's WebGL probe.

install.macos: bin/vh setup

modules.name: python-packages
modules.purpose: The libraries bin/vh's Python tools run with, fetched by uv on first use into its cache: numpy, scipy, librosa and pillow (beats, qa, music, sfx, mix profiles, sheet, storyboard, check's frame scan), jieba (captions), fonttools and brotli (fonts list, subset).
modules.license: numpy, scipy: BSD-3-Clause; librosa: ISC; pillow: MIT-CMU; jieba, fonttools, brotli: MIT

install.macos: the first bin/vh beats, qa, music, sheet or storyboard fetches them (about 700 MB)
install.linux: the first bin/vh beats, qa, music, sheet or storyboard fetches them (about 700 MB)

modules.name: latex
modules.purpose: Typesets Manim's MathTex.
modules.license: TeX Live: free software, mostly LPPL and GPL

install.macos: MacTeX: brew install --cask mactex-no-gui
install.linux: TeX Live: sudo apt install texlive-latex-extra

modules.name: manim
modules.purpose: Manim Community, the engine of math, physics and paper explainers (video types 01 and 06); each project has its own, through uv.

check.per_project: cd <project> && uv init --bare --python 3.12 && uv add manim

modules.name: manimgx
modules.purpose: ManimGX, an optional backend for Manim scenes: Manim CE's Python API on a Rust and wgpu core (Metal on macOS; Mesa's lavapipe on a Linux without a GPU), Typst for MathTex (no LaTeX), its own encoder. A uv tool, out of the projects' environments; its MP4 is conformed before the repo's checks (engines/manimgx.md).

version.tested: 0.1.1 with Python 3.13 on an M3 Max: showcase 03 about 5x as fast as Manim CE 0.21 (docs/research/08-manimgx.md)

modules.license: MIT for its own code; its native wheels bundle x264 and are GPL-3.0-or-later as a whole (its LICENSE-THIRD-PARTY); what it renders is yours

install.macos: uv tool install --python 3.13 manimgx==0.1.1

modules.name: blender
modules.purpose: Shots that need path-traced light, physics or real depth of field, and the Blender style scenes (styles/tabletop-miniature).
modules.license: GPL-2.0-or-later; this repo's scripts that import bpy are GPL-3.0-or-later; what it renders is yours

install.macos: brew install --cask blender
install.linux: blender.org's download, or your package manager

modules.name: qwen3-tts
modules.purpose: bin/vh tts's default voice: Qwen3-TTS, local, offline and free, run by mlx-audio.
modules.elsewhere: bin/vh tts takes edge, gemini, minimax, dashscope or elevenlabs here

install.macos: the first bin/vh tts with the default provider fetches it (about 2 GB) from Hugging Face

modules.name: mlx-audio
modules.purpose: Runs Qwen3-TTS on Apple Silicon for bin/vh tts's default provider.
modules.elsewhere: bin/vh tts takes edge, gemini, minimax, dashscope or elevenlabs here

install.macos: the first bin/vh tts with the default provider fetches it and its packages (about 750 MB)

modules.name: mlx-whisper
modules.purpose: Local word timing (Whisper on Apple Silicon, mlx-community/whisper-large-v3-turbo unless WHISPER_MODEL says): bin/vh tts --align local and bin/vh pace --align whisper (or local), no key and no daily quota.
modules.elsewhere: bin/vh tts takes --align gemini here, and bin/vh pace --align map (the default) or gemini

install.macos: the first bin/vh tts --align local or pace --align whisper fetches it (the model: about 1.6 GB, once)

modules.name: say
modules.purpose: macOS's own speech, bin/vh tts's say provider (drafts).
modules.elsewhere: drafts with bin/vh tts edge, or a cloud provider, here

modules.name: edge-tts
modules.purpose: Microsoft Edge's online voices through the edge-tts package, no key: bin/vh tts edge.
modules.license: the package: LGPL-3.0; the voices: Microsoft's service, unofficial

install.macos: the first bin/vh tts edge fetches it
install.linux: the first bin/vh tts edge fetches it

modules.name: gemini
modules.purpose: Google's Gemini API: bin/vh tts gemini and gemini-lite, word timing with --align gemini (tts, pace), the voice library and voice design (voices), pictures (image gen: Nano Banana 2.1 for drafts, Nano Banana Pro for finals) and music (music --provider lyria: Lyria 3.5), both through the Interactions API.
modules.license: Google's Gemini API terms; its speech carries an inaudible SynthID watermark, so AI narration is disclosed (NOTES.md); so do its pictures (image gen: AIGC on record)

needs.account: a Google AI Studio API key; the free tier has a daily quota

modules.name: minimax
modules.purpose: MiniMax's T2A v2 speech: bin/vh tts minimax, with word timing from its own subtitles.

needs.account: the international platform (platform.minimax.io): a Token Plan key spends its credits, a pay-as-you-go key the account's balance; a China-platform key needs MINIMAX_BASE_URL=https://api.minimaxi.com

hints.1004: a key of the other platform? MINIMAX_BASE_URL picks it
hints.2049: a key of the other platform? MINIMAX_BASE_URL picks it

modules.name: elevenlabs
modules.purpose: ElevenLabs speech with timestamps: bin/vh tts elevenlabs.

needs.account: an ElevenLabs account and API key

modules.name: dashscope
modules.purpose: Alibaba Cloud Model Studio speech through the dashscope SDK: bin/vh tts dashscope.
modules.license: Alibaba Cloud's terms; the SDK: Apache-2.0

needs.account: an Alibaba Cloud Model Studio key; the international site needs DASHSCOPE_BASE_URL=https://dashscope-intl.aliyuncs.com/api/v1

modules.name: internet-archive
modules.purpose: Internet Archive's search and item metadata: bin/vh footage search archive, files and get (newsreels, government films; each item's own licence decides).
modules.license: Internet Archive's terms of use; every item carries its own rights (licenseurl, rights), which footage classifies

needs.account: none: the search and download endpoints need no key

modules.name: wikimedia-commons
modules.purpose: Wikimedia Commons' MediaWiki API: bin/vh footage search commons, files and get (each file page's LicenseShortName and LicenseUrl).
modules.license: the Wikimedia Foundation's terms; each file under the licence its page states

needs.account: none: the API asks only for a User-Agent that names the tool (tools/assets/fetch.py sends one)

modules.name: nasa-images
modules.purpose: NASA's Image and Video Library API (images-api.nasa.gov): bin/vh footage search nasa, files and get, renditions up to ~orig.
modules.license: NASA's media usage guidelines (www.nasa.gov/nasa-brand-center/images-and-media/, checked 2026-10-26): NASA's own media are generally not subject to copyright in the U.S.; credit NASA, no insignia, no implied endorsement; third-party material is marked with its holder

needs.account: none: the library's API needs no key (api.nasa.gov's other APIs do; footage does not call them)

modules.name: openverse
modules.purpose: Openverse's audio search (api.openverse.org): bin/vh sfx search and pick (Freesound's effects, an HQ preview MP3 each), bgm search and pick (Jamendo's music), with each item's licence, credit line and page.
modules.license: Openverse's terms (WordPress.org); every item under the licence its source gives (CC0, CC BY …), which the tools classify

needs.account: none: anonymous clients get 20 searches a minute and 200 a day (the x-ratelimit headers); a registered app gets more

modules.name: codex
modules.purpose: OpenAI's Codex CLI, an agent that reads AGENTS.md; bin/vh install-skill codex puts the skill where it looks (~/.agents/skills); bin/vh image gen --provider codex runs its image_gen (codex exec, read-only sandbox) on the ChatGPT plan it is signed in with.

needs.account: a ChatGPT sign-in or an OpenAI API key

install.macos: npm install -g @openai/codex, then bin/vh install-skill codex
install.linux: npm install -g @openai/codex, then bin/vh install-skill codex

modules.name: claude-code
modules.purpose: Anthropic's Claude Code, an agent that reads CLAUDE.md; bin/vh install-skill claude puts the skill where it looks (~/.claude/skills).

needs.account: a Claude subscription or an Anthropic API key

install.macos: claude.com/claude-code, then bin/vh install-skill claude

modules.name: yt-dlp
modules.purpose: Reads video sites: scout and ref take a search's, a channel's or one video's metadata from YouTube with it (-J, never a download; OVH_YTDLP runs another, uvx yt-dlp). Sites change often, so an old one is the first thing to update when a site fails.

install.macos: brew upgrade yt-dlp, or brew install yt-dlp
install.linux: uv tool upgrade yt-dlp, or uv tool install yt-dlp

modules.name: fxtwitter
modules.purpose: FixTweet's public API for X (api.fxtwitter.com/2): a profile's latest statuses with their views, likes and the followers, one status, the trends; no login and no key (scout channel, post and hot; ref add).
modules.license: the service's terms (FixTweet's code is MIT); the posts are their authors'

modules.name: bilibili-view
modules.purpose: Bilibili's public view endpoint for one video (its counts, date and uploader) and the uploader's follower count (scout post, ref add). Search, popular and ranking answer a risk-control code without a browser's cookies: they are read in the built-in browser, never signed or worked round.
modules.license: Bilibili's terms; the videos are their uploaders'

modules.name: baidu-top
modules.purpose: Baidu's realtime hot-search board (top.baidu.com), the first list of scout hot.

modules.name: toutiao-hot
modules.purpose: Toutiao's hot board (toutiao.com/hot-event), a list of scout hot.

modules.name: google-trends
modules.purpose: Google Trends' daily trending searches as RSS (trends.google.com/trending/rss), by region: a list of scout hot.
